title: Cloud Security — Secure After You Share

steps.title: Welcome to the Lab
steps.instruction:
Welcome to the Secure After You Share lab. You will investigate a prepared pull request, harden its GitHub Actions workflow, triage cloud security signals, evaluate Copilot code review, and make an evidence-based merge decision.

This is a challenge lab. Use the disposable repository and prepared pull request provided for class.

steps.title: Inspect the Workflow Delta
steps.instruction:
We've opened the Explorer. Find the changed workflow under .github/workflows. Identify its trigger, token permissions, third-party actions, event-derived inputs, secrets, and runner.

Challenge: describe one path where untrusted pull-request content could influence privileged execution.

steps.title: Record the Threat Model
steps.instruction:
Create docs/cloud-security-review.md with these headings:
• # Pull request intent
• ## Workflow trust boundary
• ## Security signals
• ## Review decisions
• ## Merge decision

Record the workflow threat, available privilege, and likely impact.

steps.title: Check the Threat Model
steps.instruction: Run Check Mission Progress. Your review should identify both the workflow's intended behavior and the boundary where untrusted data meets privilege.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the Explorer for you.

For future reference:
• Explorer: Ctrl+Shift+E

steps.title: Propose the Smallest Complete Hardening
steps.instruction:
Revise the workflow so pull-request validation keeps only the authority it needs. Consider explicit token permissions, pinned action references, safe handling of event data, and separation of privileged deployment.

Preserve the workflow's intended validation behavior. Record the control and residual risk in docs/cloud-security-review.md.

steps.title: Validate the Workflow
steps.instruction:
We've opened the Terminal. Inspect the revised diff and run the repository's workflow lint or validation command if one is available. Use git diff --check as a minimum formatting check.

Do not push until you can explain why every remaining permission is required.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the terminal for you.

For future reference:
• Terminal: Ctrl+`

steps.title: Trace the CodeQL Result
steps.instruction:
Open the prepared CodeQL alert in the pull request. Record the query, severity, untrusted source, propagation steps, missing control, sensitive sink, and affected commit.

Decide whether the path is reachable before selecting a remediation.

steps.title: Compare with Autofix
steps.instruction: If a Copilot Autofix suggestion is available, compare it with the complete source-to-sink path. Record whether you would accept, revise, or reject the patch and what validation your decision requires.

steps.title: Classify Every Cloud Signal
steps.instruction:
In docs/cloud-security-review.md, add one entry for each prepared signal:
• CodeQL data-flow alert
• Secret scanning alert or push-protection event
• Dependency review finding
• License policy change

For each entry, record the evidence, immediate response, owner, and merge impact.

steps.title: Check Signal Ownership
steps.instruction: Run Check Mission Progress. The review must distinguish credential response from code remediation and dependency risk instead of treating every finding as the same kind of failure.

steps.title: Request Copilot Code Review
steps.instruction: Use the prepared pull request to request Copilot code review. While the review runs, inspect the pull-request description and repository instructions. Identify which security expectations are explicit and which context is missing.

steps.title: Try to Falsify a Comment
steps.instruction:
Choose one Copilot comment. Trace the relevant code path and inspect existing controls. Classify the claim as confirmed, needs evidence, or unsupported.

Record the evidence and your proposed response in docs/cloud-security-review.md.

steps.title: Design the Merge Ruleset
steps.instruction:
Draft a merge policy for this repository. Name the required Actions and code-scanning checks, dependency threshold, approval requirement, stale-approval behavior, and authorized bypass role.

Every rule should address a risk identified in this pull request. Avoid adding checks that have no owner or response path.

steps.title: Check the Policy
steps.instruction: Run Check Mission Progress. Your review record should define required checks, human approval, and exception handling clearly enough for another repository administrator to implement.

steps.title: Inspect the Current Commit
steps.instruction: We've opened the Terminal. Run gh pr checks, gh pr diff, and gh pr view. Confirm that required checks apply to the current pull-request commit and that no material change landed after the latest approval.

steps.title: Record the Merge Decision
steps.instruction:
Complete ## Merge decision with one choice: approve, request changes, or block and escalate. Cite the workflow, code, secret, dependency, review, and policy evidence supporting that choice.

Stop before merge unless you are the authorized approver for this disposable repository.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the terminal for you.

For future reference:
• Terminal: Ctrl+`

steps.title: Lab Complete!
steps.instruction:
Congratulations! You completed the cloud security challenge.

You practiced:
• Threat-modeling and hardening a GitHub Actions workflow
• Applying least privilege, pinned actions, OIDC, and environments
• Tracing CodeQL evidence and evaluating Autofix
• Responding correctly to exposed secrets
• Reviewing dependency and license changes
• Verifying Copilot code review comments
• Designing enforceable merge policy
• Using security campaigns to coordinate remediation at scale
• Preserving human ownership of the final decision
